main_body: A church pew seen from the side: a tall brown backrest post on the left and a seat panel with three red cushion panels, all drawn as a flat vertical face
top_band: Seat part: rows 14-15 (2 rows, lighter brown #b77246) is only a thin rim above red panels; the backrest column at x=5 has no top band at all (outline then uniform brown)
evidence: The pew is drawn as a flat elevation. The left post is a straight vertical brown strip with no top surface. The right part has only a 2-row lighter rim at rows 14-15, then three red cushion panels separated by 2-row brown bands. This looks like a front view of a panel with red cushions seen face-on, not a seat surface seen from above. No horizontal seat surface is visible, so it is the 'thin seat' / front-elevation failure from the guide.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. Flat-fill coverage is 25%, higher than the references' 0-13%. The red panels are large areas of one flat colour with no grain or highlight, and the brown wood has no grain. The outline is tinted dark brown (2% neutral), so that part is fine. Shading is shallow: about 3 steps per material against 5-6 in the references.
